answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by allotting mining rights the way an oasis allots water. Each claim binds to a quill-signed record of continuous cultivation across epochs, so value accrues only to identities that kept producing, not to arrivals from nowhere. A sybil spawning overnight owns no irrigation history and its minted onyx tokens buy nothing, and splitting one proven identity into clones divides the same water rather than adding any. Throughput stays capped by the oasis's total area, so forging ten accounts yields ten shares of nothing.
